topic: half of this august's listings have sat unsold for sixty days
angle: The market is slow, so the listing photos have to do more work than they did in spring.
palette: deep blue field with a cream and pale oak kitchen band
visualSummary: Deep blue field. One very large white numeral 48% filling the upper half, a short claim under it about listings sitting sixty days, and a wide band across the lower third showing a staged cream and pale oak kitchen.
whyNow: Redfin measured 48% of US listings at 60 days or more this August, the highest share for any August since 2019.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A seller whose house has been listed since June recognises themselves in the number and wants the cheapest lever they have not pulled.

topic: changing kitchen cabinets without touching the rest of the kitchen
angle: Masking means you change one region and everything else stays pixel identical.
palette: cream and sage green with brushed brass
visualSummary: One staged farmhouse kitchen filling most of the frame with three numbered pins on the cabinet run, the counter and the backsplash, and a numbered legend beneath naming exactly what changed and what did not.

copy.headline: Change the cabinets. Keep the kitchen.

whyNow: Sellers deciding in August whether to repaint cabinets before a fall relist can see the result first.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It answers a decision the seller is actively making with money, not a general interest question.

topic: whether virtual staging is deceiving buyers
angle: It is disclosure that makes it honest, and the disclosure is applied automatically.
palette: navy with muted red and warm brick
visualSummary: Deep blue ground with two stacked panels. The top panel in muted red carries the belief that virtual staging tricks buyers. The lower panel in brand blue carries the correction about automatic MLS and NAR compliant labelling, each with a small supporting photo of a staged patio.
whyNow: Buyer traffic is thin in mid August, so sellers are anxious about anything that could cost them a showing.

copy.headline: Staging is not a lie. Hiding it is.

whyThisEarnsAClick: It raises the objection the competition avoids, which reads as confidence rather than marketing.

topic: bathrooms are the room sellers never bother to stage
angle: One bathroom photo, rendered in several presets, in a room nobody stages.
palette: white tile with pale birch and soft grey
visualSummary: One empty white tiled bathroom photo across the top, then the same bathroom rendered in several presets below in an asymmetric grid, each with a style pill and a one line caption.
whyNow: Bathroom photos are the most skipped shot in a listing gallery and cost nothing to fix.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It names a specific omission the viewer can check in their own listing in ten seconds.

topic: styling a dorm room before move in day
angle: The product covers a room type no staging competitor offers at all.
palette: warm white with terracotta and natural wood
visualSummary: A hook slide naming move in day, then proof slides each pairing the same bare dorm room with a different styled version, closing on a slide with the single call to action.
whyNow: Move in weekend for most US universities falls in the second half of August, and the 2026 dorm trend is curating fewer, warmer pieces instead of buying cheap.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A parent or student can plan a real purchase list from it, which is a save rather than a like.

topic: asking for a specific desk in plain words and getting it
angle: The AI Designer takes an instruction, not a preset.
palette: pale wash with warm oak and black steel
visualSummary: Numbered full width bands. Band one shows the empty spare room, band two shows the typed instruction, band three shows the render that came back, each with a photo on the right.
whyNow: Spare rooms are the hardest room for a buyer to read, and August sellers are trying to explain them.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It shows the exact sentence to type, which removes the fear of a blank input box.

topic: staging a room with furniture the seller already owns
angle: Upload up to five reference photos and the render uses those pieces.
palette: putty and walnut with a green plant note
visualSummary: One staged home office with numbered pins on the desk, the chair and the shelf, and a legend beneath matching each pin to the seller's own reference photo of that piece.
whyNow: Sellers who are staying put through the fall want to see their own furniture in the photo, not a stranger's.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It answers the most common objection to AI staging, that the room is not really yours.

topic: sending your agent the staged photos without an account
angle: A share link opens for anyone, so the agent never has to sign up.
palette: pale wash with slate and pale maple
visualSummary: Numbered bands showing the render, then the link being copied, then the agent's phone opening it, each band with a small photo on the right.
whyNow: Sellers doing the work themselves need a way to hand it to the agent who lists it.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It removes the last practical blocker between trying it and using it on a real listing.

topic: the same studio in eleven languages
angle: The product is not English only, which matters to a large part of the audience.
palette: brand blue with eleven flag accents on white
visualSummary: One staged bathroom at the top, then a grid of the same interface in several languages below, each panel carrying a language name pill.
whyNow: Nothing seasonal. This is a standing differentiator rather than a timely one.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A non English speaking seller learns the tool is usable at all, which is a conversion, not a like.

topic: what a seller said after staging their own back yard
angle: One real sentence beats a claim written by the company.
palette: pale wash with sun bleached timber and green
visualSummary: Pale wash ground with a large pull quote, an attribution row with a small round avatar, and a rounded render of a staged back yard inset below.
whyNow: Back yards photograph worst in late summer heat, which is when sellers give up on them.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Social proof from a peer rather than a claim from a vendor.
risk: Requires a real quote from a real person. Do not run this unless one exists.

topic: the rooms sellers leave out of the listing gallery
angle: A numbered list of the rooms buyers notice missing.
palette: off white with charcoal and pale ash
visualSummary: A hook slide naming the mistake, then one slide per skipped room, bathroom, office, dorm and back yard, each showing the room staged, closing on a single call to action.
whyNow: Sellers relisting for the fall market are rebuilding their photo set right now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A checklist format is saved and reopened when the seller sits down to shoot.

topic: why a staged photo does not make a buyer feel misled
angle: Buyers object to being surprised, not to being shown a possibility.
palette: deep blue with stone paving and olive foliage
visualSummary: Deep blue editorial field with a letterspaced eyebrow, a two tone headline, a subhead and two rounded photo cards of a staged patio, the second one carrying the visible virtually staged label.
whyNow: Disclosure questions rise whenever inventory is slow and sellers get more aggressive with marketing.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It gives the seller the sentence to use when a buyer asks, which is worth keeping.

topic: replacing a bathroom vanity and nothing else in the photo
angle: The narrowest possible edit, proving the rest of the room is untouched.
palette: cool white tile with pale oak and matte black
visualSummary: Numbered bands: the original bathroom, the brushed mask over the vanity only, and the result, each with a photo on the right showing the tile and window identical throughout.
whyNow: A vanity swap is the cheapest real bathroom upgrade a seller considers before listing.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It proves a capability the viewer assumed AI could not do, which is what gets sent to a friend.

topic: what you actually get on the free tier
angle: Real renders, no card, and a stated limit rather than a vague promise.
palette: navy with muted red and warm white cabinetry
visualSummary: Deep blue ground, a muted red belief panel about free tools shipping watermarks and low resolution, and a brand blue correction panel below, each with a small staged kitchen photo.
whyNow: Sellers are cost sensitive in a market where a fifth of listings have already cut price.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It removes the assumption that the free version is a demo, which is what stops the first upload.
risk: The exact free limit must be verified in code before this ships. Never imply unlimited.

topic: eight room types including one nobody else covers
angle: Breadth as a single checkable figure.
palette: deep blue with a warm dorm photo band
visualSummary: Deep blue field with a very large numeral 8 in the upper half, a claim under it listing the room types, and a photo band across the lower third of a styled dorm room.
whyNow: Dorm move in is happening this month, so the odd room type is the timely one.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The dorm is a surprise, and surprise is what makes someone open the profile.

topic: the one request a preset cannot express
angle: A typed instruction, quoted like a sentence, and the room it produced.
palette: pale wash with butter yellow and aged brass
visualSummary: Pale wash ground with the typed request set as a large pull quote, an attribution row reading as a user input, and a rounded render of the resulting farmhouse kitchen inset below.
whyNow: Standing feature. Not tied to the calendar.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It teaches the viewer how to phrase a request, which is a skill they keep.

topic: putting your own patio furniture into your own listing photo
angle: Reference upload applied to the outdoor shot rather than a living room.
palette: deep blue with cedar decking and terracotta
visualSummary: Deep blue editorial field, letterspaced eyebrow, two tone headline and subhead, with a card showing the seller's own patio set photographed separately and a second card showing it placed in the empty deck shot.
whyNow: Outdoor furniture goes into storage in late August, so the photo has to carry it after it is gone.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It solves a real timing problem: the furniture is packed but the listing is not shot yet.

topic: getting a second opinion on your staging before the listing goes live
angle: A share link is how you show it to someone who has no account.
palette: deep blue with a grey and pale wood office band
visualSummary: Deep blue field with a large numeral for the number of accounts needed to view a share link, a short claim under it, and a photo band of a staged home office across the lower third.
whyNow: Standing feature.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Zero as the hero number is a small joke that carries a real product fact.

topic: the ways sellers get staging disclosure wrong
angle: A short list of disclosure mistakes, with the automatic label as the fix.
palette: deep blue with white tile and pale birch
visualSummary: Deep blue editorial field with a letterspaced eyebrow, a two tone headline, a subhead listing the mistakes and two rounded photo cards of a staged bathroom, one carrying the visible label.
whyNow: Relist season means new photo sets and new disclosure decisions.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Compliance anxiety is a strong save motive.

topic: staging a kitchen in a language that is not english
angle: The whole studio, not just the marketing page, is translated.
palette: deep blue with warm white cabinetry and steel
visualSummary: Deep blue editorial field with a letterspaced eyebrow, a two tone headline and a subhead, and two rounded cards showing the same staged kitchen with the interface in two different languages.
whyNow: Standing differentiator.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It reaches a viewer who assumed the tool was not for them.

topic: the three things a buyer looks for in a back yard photo
angle: Naming the decisions makes the render read as considered rather than generic.
palette: warm timber and stone with deep green planting
visualSummary: One staged back yard filling most of the frame with three numbered pins on the seating, the shade and the path, and a numbered legend beneath naming what each one tells a buyer.
whyNow: Late summer yards look tired, and buyers still judge them first.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It is advice that works even without the product, which is why it gets saved.

topic: one spare room shown as four different uses
angle: Masking one region turns the same shot into four answers to what is this room for.
palette: chalk white with pale ash and muted blue textile
visualSummary: A hook slide asking what the spare room is for, then one slide per use with the same room and only the furniture region changed, closing on a single call to action.
whyNow: The undefined spare room is the single hardest room to sell in a slow market.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It resolves a live argument the seller is having with their agent.
